rationale: The question is the prevalence of missed care and its association with the staffing of the shift described, at one point in time: a cross-sectional survey with linkage to scheduling and acuity records measures exactly that. The conflict between c2 and c3 is addressed by measuring acuity for the same shift rather than as a unit average. Reporting follows STROBE for cross-sectional studies.
alternatives: Repeated monthly survey panel (refused: the budget question needs one snapshot, and repeated surveys fatigue staff)
Direct observation of care (refused: costly, reactive and impossible across 18 units in four weeks)
Survey without scheduling linkage (refused: relies on nurses' recall of staffing)
whyNotMoreComplex: A longitudinal design would add little to a budget decision and would need repeated paid time the union has not agreed.

decision.statement: Run the last-shift cross-sectional survey on all 18 units in a four-week winter window during paid time, linking each response to the planned and actual hours and the acuity of the shift described, because shift shortfalls have been linked to missed care (c1, c3), protected time makes a usable response rate realistic (c4), and the checklist needs a pretest with licensed practical nurses (c5).
decision.question: Should the hospital run a last-shift missed care survey linked to shift staffing and acuity this winter?

criteria.text: Below-plan shifts have been associated with more missed care in linked or multi-hospital data.
Acuity fully explains the staffing association where units staff to acuity.

gates.requirement: REB approval of the survey protocol
gates.evidence: REB approval REB-26-1182 dated 2026-09-15, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Union agreement to paid time for survey completion
gates.evidence: Union letter UL-114 dated 2026-09-08 granting 20 minutes of paid time, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Survey without linkage to scheduling records
Direct observation of care on a sample of shifts
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1, c3, c4 and c5; the conflicting claim c2 is carried in the defeating criterion, whose status stays unknown until the survey is analysed. Both gates are met on investigator-supplied letters.

summary: Cross-sectional linked survey recommended; both gates are met on investigator-supplied letters.
